body:
h1. Unified Inference â€” Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes

Short intro
This page consolidates the canonical product definition and execution plan for Unified Inference (UIF). It includes the product overview, prioritized requirements (PRD), high-level design notes for the serving runtime and control plane, roadmap and themes through Q2 2027, pricing and packaging guidance for GA, and the release notes and rollout plan for the 2026-10-10 release (v2026.10).

h2. Product overview
Purpose: Provide a unified LLM inference platform that delivers predictable latency, cost controls, and consistent developer experience across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
Key capabilities:
- Text generation & chat (streaming, function calling)
- Embeddings and similarity search endpoints
- Model catalog with version pinning and verified performance profiles
- Smart routing (cost/latency/region policies) and graceful fallback to compatible variants
- Redwood Optimize integrations for quantization and batching recommendations

Primary customers and use cases:
- AI-first startups: rapid prototyping and production with predictable latency
- Enterprise product teams: SLA-backed Dedicated and Private options for regulated workloads
- Platform teams: consistent runtime across business units, centralized cost controls

h2. Goals and success metrics (North Star)
Primary goal: Reduce customer inference cost by 30% (median) while meeting 99th-percentile latency SLOs for interactive workloads.
Success metrics (12-month):
1. P50 token latency for chat endpoints <= 120ms (hosted small models), P99 <= 450ms.
2. Average cost-per-1k-tokens reduced 30% vs. baseline (model + infra).
3. Developer time-to-first-call < 10 minutes (quickstart + credits).
4. 99.95% uptime for Dedicated clusters with automated failover.
5. NPS of product users >= 45 for DX/SDK experience.

h2. PRD â€” Requirements (prioritized)
Intro: The following are the minimal and extended requirements for the next GA release. Each item lists owner and acceptance criteria.

Table: Requirements (columns: id | title | priority | owner | acceptance_criteria)
- R-001 | Core REST/SDK endpoints (generate, chat, embeddings, rerank) | Must | product/eng-dx | Endpoints available with stable schema; SDK call in <10s; sample app runs end-to-end.
- R-002 | Model catalog & version pinning | Must | eng-platform | Users can pin to model:vX; rollout supports canary + automatic fallback.
- R-003 | Smart routing policies | High | eng-serving-runtime | Policy types: latency, cost, region. Default policy enforceable at route-level.
- R-004 | Observability & cost breakdown | Must | eng-platform | Token-level cost and latency breakdowns visible in Console; per-route dashboards created.
- R-005 | Dedicated capacity launch (beta) | High | infra/eng-dedicated | Reserved GPU pools, commit billing, SLA page published.
- R-006 | Redwood Optimize integration (batching/quant) | Medium | research/applied-ml | Auto-suggest configs with expected cost delta estimate.
- R-007 | Private (VPC) deployment checklist | High | eng-private-deployments | Launch checklist, KMS integration, audit logs, and support runbooks completed.

Acceptance criteria notes:
- Each Must/High item must have end-to-end e2e test in CI, PR review, and an associated runbook for operations.

h2. Design specifications (high level)
This section captures the design decisions that engineering teams must follow. For detailed ADRs, see linked ADRs in related_pages.

h3. Runtime & kernel selection
- Kernel selection based on model architecture, sequence length distribution, and hardware capability.
- Runtime will maintain a profile registry per model variant containing: default batch size, preferred kernel set, kv-cache memory estimate, and quantization support.

h3. Smart routing component
- Policy engine evaluates per-request metadata (route, customer tier, region, latency budget, and cost tags).
- Routing decision flow (simplified): 1) Check route policy; 2) If capacity constrained, evaluate fallback list ordered by compatibility and cost; 3) Return selection and record decision for telemetry.

h3. Caching & batching
- Automatic prefix/KV caching at per-customer scope with TTL and size limits.
- Batching scheduler uses adaptive time-windowing up to configured max latency (default 15ms) and model-specific max batch size.

h3. API changes (examples)
- New route-level config JSON (example):
{
  "route": "/chat",
  "policy": { "type": "latency", "latency_budget_ms": 300, "fallbacks": ["gpt-small", "gpt-medium-quant"] },
  "cache": { "enabled": true, "ttl_s": 3600 }
}

h2. Observability & SLOs
- SLO targets:
  - Hosted API availability: 99.9% monthly
  - Dedicated cluster availability (SLA): 99.95% monthly
  - Error budget policy: production services use 5% monthly error budget; automatic throttling and rollback policies are defined in runbooks.
- Telemetry events required:
  - request.start, request.end (latency_ms, route, model_variant)
  - cost.charge (tokens, unit_cost, infra_cost)
  - routing.decision (policy, selected_variant, fallback_used boolean)

h2. Roadmap & themes (Q4 2026 â€” Q2 2027)
Themes by priority:
- Q4 2026 (Launch GA): Hosted GA + Dedicated beta, Console cost dashboards, model catalog + routing policies.
- Q1 2027 (Optimization): Redwood Optimize v2, auto-quant recommendations, workload-based batching presets.
- Q2 2027 (Enterprise readiness): Private deployments (VPC/on-prem), advanced KMS/HSM integrations, per-tenant fine-grained RBAC.

Milestones (timeline):
1. 2026-10-10 â€” v2026.10 (GA candidate): core endpoints, routing policies, console dashboards, Dedicated beta docs.
2. 2026-11-30 â€” v2026.11: Dedicated GA (commit billing), expanded model catalog.
3. 2027-02-15 â€” v2027.02: Redwood Optimize v2 with quantization autosuggest.
4. 2027-05-01 â€” v2027.05: Private deployment GA (VPC) and enterprise compliance bundle.

h2. Pricing & packaging notes
Goal: Align price with measurable unit economics while offering predictable spend for enterprise customers.
Guiding principles:
- Usage-based baseline for Hosted (per-token generation + embedding-unit pricing).
- Commit-based reserved pricing for Dedicated (monthly/annual commitments with tiered discounts).
- Private: platform fee + support tier; negotiating with enterprise customers for on-prem license.

Proposed GA pricing tiers (illustrative):
Table: Pricing (tier | hosted per-1k tokens gen | embeddings per-1k | reserved discount)
- Developer / Starter | $0.60 | $0.80 | NA
- Business | $0.45 | $0.60 | 10% on 3-month commit
- Enterprise | $0.30 | $0.40 | 20-40% on annual reserved Dedicated capacity

Add-ons and enterprise features:
- Extended observability retention (30/90/365 days) â€” add-on
- Compliance & audit package (SOC2, ISO evidence) â€” enterprise feature
- Premium SLA and dedicated support â€” negotiable

Billing notes for engineering:
- Token-metering must be deterministic and idempotent across retries. Meter must record model_variant, sequence_length, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens.
- Offline billing reconciliation job runs daily with drift threshold alerts (>0.5% drift).

h2. Release notes â€” v2026.10 (2026-10-10)
Highlights:
- GA candidate of Unified Inference Hosted API: generate, chat (streaming), embeddings.
- Model catalog with version pinning and per-variant performance profiles.
- Route-level smart routing policies: latency/cost/region and fallback lists.
- Console: per-route token/cost/latency dashboards and first-class traces for requests.
- Dedicated capacity beta: reserved GPU pools, commit UI, and SLA doc (beta).

Breaking changes:
- None for the GA candidate; schema additions are backward-compatible.

Known issues & workarounds:
- Large embedding batch memory spike observed at >50k tokens per-batch (issue tracker: INF-422). Workaround: cap batch-size to 4k tokens for large models in tenant cfg.
- Occasional 502 from a canary rollout in specialized GPU regions due to container image mismatch (INF-438). Ops workaround: auto-rollback to previous image version and alert image curator.

h2. Rollout plan and launch checklist
Pre-launch (T-3 weeks):
1. Complete e2e test matrix and load test for 1k rps (owner: eng-serving-runtime).
2. Security review and penetration test (owner: security-and-compliance).
3. Billing & metering validation (owner: finance-and-legal).
4. Sales enablement materials & pricing sheet (owner: sales-enablement).

Launch-day (2026-10-10):
1. Open hosted endpoints with feature flags off for 5% of traffic; monitor routing.decision and cost.
2. Increase to 25% at hour 2, 75% at hour 8, 100% at day 1 if SLOs hold.
3. Activate Dedicated beta UI and notify early access customers.

Post-launch (T+1 week):
1. Run canary analysis and automated regression checks against eval prompt-sets.
2. Collect initial customer feedback and track support SLAs.

h2. Appendix (configs & examples)
1) Example SDK call (Node):
const resp = await redwoodClient.chat.create({
  route: '/chat',
  model: 'gpt-medium',
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Summarize the Q3 roadmap' }],
  stream: true
});

2) Route policy example (YAML):
route: /chat
policy:
  type: latency
  latency_budget_ms: 300
  fallbacks: [gpt-medium, gpt-small-quant]
cache:
  enabled: true
  ttl_s: 3600
